headline: Bill Gates said companies that replace a worker with a robot should pay into the pension system, reviving his 'tax the robots' idea.
score_reason: Lowered from 6: the interview was given the week before 6 Oct 2026, and this report mainly surveys the wider tax debate.
importance_line: The idea could affect pensions and jobs if adopted, but it is a proposal by a private citizen with no legislation behind it; US bills on AI taxes have made little headway.
source: EL PAÍS English, citing The New York Times
summary: EL PAÍS English reports that Gates, in an interview with Ezra Klein of The New York Times last week, asked why a company that replaces a worker with a robot should not also pay into the pension fund that workers support. EL PAÍS adds that progressive US lawmakers have introduced about six proposals to tax AI companies, which have made little headway because Democrats control neither chamber of Congress.
notes: Times of India page returned no text; read EL PAÍS on the same story. El PAÍS says only 'last week' for the NYT interview, so the exact date is unknown and the event is probably before 6 Oct; hence no precise FOLLOW-UP date. Gates first proposed robot taxes in 2017 (per the headline).
